paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “In an era of rapid social development, it is vitally important to enhance young people’s sense of responsibility.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：这一部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“在社会快速发展的时代，增强年轻人的责任感至关重要”。您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Imagine you and a stranger are sitting on a couch. How close would you sit to them? It turns out that how much of a 26 zone you prefer may reveal a lot about your personality.
paragraphs.translationZh: 想象一下你和一个陌生人坐在沙发上。你会坐得离他们多近？事实证明，你喜欢多少缓冲区可能会透露出你的性格。

paragraphs.sourceText: In one study, researchers sought to 27 how our personality may be linked to our preferred amount of personal space. The researchers found that people who scored higher in the 28 of agreeableness tended to sit closer to others, as did people who were more open and outgoing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一项研究中，研究人员试图确定我们的个性与我们偏好的个人空间大小之间的关系。研究人员发现，在宜人性特征上得分较高的人倾向于与他人坐得更近，而性格更开放、外向的人也是如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: Other individual differences, such as gender and age, can also affect how much personal space we 29 . Women tend to prefer more physical distance from strangers or acquaintances and older adults also generally tend to prefer to keep more distance between themselves and others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 其他个体差异，例如性别和年龄，也会影响我们渴望多少个人空间。女性倾向于与陌生人或熟人保持更大的身体距离，而老年人通常也倾向于与他人保持更大的距离。

paragraphs.sourceText: Beyond reflecting our personality and 30 , the amount of personal space we prefer is also linked to our cultural backgrounds. In a study involving participants from 42 countries, researchers found that around the world people’s desired amount of personal space varied 31 . For example, in Romania, the average amount of personal space people said they would prefer from a stranger was more than 4 feet, whereas in Argentina it was roughly half that.
paragraphs.translationZh: 除了反映我们的个性和人口统计数据之外，我们喜欢的个人空间大小还与我们的文化背景有关。在一项涉及来自 42 个国家/地区的参与者的研究中，研究人员发现世界各地人们所需的个人空间存在很大差异。例如，在罗马尼亚，人们表示他们更愿意与陌生人拥有超过 4 英尺的个人空间，而在阿根廷，这一数字大约只有一半。

paragraphs.sourceText: What might 32 this variation? The researchers looked at a number of 33 factors, but the only one that was significantly 34 with preferred interpersonal distance was average temperature. The warmer the place, it seems, the “warmer” the people and the less space they needed between them and others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种变化的背后可能是什么？研究人员研究了许多潜在因素，但唯一与偏好的人际距离显着相关的是平均温度。地方越温暖，人们似乎就越“温暖”，他们与他人之间需要的空间就越少。

paragraphs.sourceText: Personal space may also reflect interpersonal attraction. Researchers have found that our chosen physical 35 also appears to reflect how much we like others. The more people would like to be friends with the other person, the closer they sat to them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 个人空间也可能反映人际吸引力。研究人员发现，我们选择的身体接近程度似乎也反映了我们对他人的喜爱程度。人们越愿意与对方成为朋友，他们与对方的距离就越近。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s Never Too Early to Teach Children about Money
paragraphs.translationZh: 教孩子金钱永远不会太早

paragraphs.sourceText: A) The cost of a mortgage or rents, meeting monthly utility bills, paying for a new car — all headaches most people get to worry about from their 20s. But while some may struggle to pay their bills after a few too many nights out at the start of the month, others will have a tightly followed plan for their repayments. So what is the difference between the shrewd saver and the more reckless spender?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 抵押贷款或租金的费用、每月的水电费、购买新车的费用——所有这些都是大多数人从 20 多岁起就开始担心的问题。不过，虽然有些人可能会在月初外出数晚后难以支付账单，但其他人则会有严格的还款计划。那么精明的储蓄者和鲁莽的花钱者有什么区别呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) Experts believe it is all about the age you learn how to spend responsibly. Adult money habits are typically set by the age of seven, according to a large-scale study by the government’s Money Advice Service and behaviour experts at Cambridge University. By then, most children have grasped how to recognise the value of money and are capable of complex functions such as planning ahead, delaying a decision until later and understanding that some choices are irreversible.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 专家认为，这完全取决于您学习如何负责任地消费的年龄。根据政府理财咨询服务机构和剑桥大学行为专家的一项大规模研究，成年人的理财习惯通常在七岁时就形成了。到那时，大多数孩子已经掌握了如何认识金钱的价值，并能够执行复杂的功能，例如提前计划、推迟决定以及理解某些选择是不可逆转的。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Tomorrow marks the start of Global Money Week, a worldwide initiative to help children make smart financial decisions and learn that “money matters matter”. But for many young people in the UK, it’s a matter of too little, too late. “The habits of mind which influence the ways children approach complex problems and decisions, including financial ones, are largely determined in the first few years of life,” says Dr David Whitebread, the co-author of the study. And this core behaviour is very likely to influence their financial decisions when they are adults, he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 明天标志着全球理财周的开始，这是一项全球性倡议，旨在帮助儿童做出明智的财务决策并了解“金钱很重要”。但对于英国的许多年轻人来说，这太少、太晚了。该研究的合著者大卫·怀特布莱德博士表示：“影响儿童处理复杂问题和决策（包括财务问题）的思维习惯在很大程度上是在生命的最初几年决定的。”他说，这种核心行为很可能会影响他们成年后的财务决策。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The study also urges parents not to underestimate their own good and bad money habits. “Since young children have few monetary resources they control independently, it is the basic approaches and skills which are modelled, discussed and demonstrated by parents that are likely to be influential levers, breeding efficient habits and practices,” it says.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 该研究还敦促父母不要低估自己的好和坏的金钱习惯。报告称：“由于幼儿几乎没有独立控制的货币资源，因此父母示范、讨论和展示的基本方法和技能很可能成为有影响力的杠杆，培养高效的习惯和做法。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Parents who choose to help their children learn how to plan ahead, reflect on the past and self-regulate car make a huge difference in promoting good financial behaviour in the future, explains Whitebread. According to a survey by M&G Investments, the vast majority (83%) of parents recognise the value of teaching their children about money. However, this concern does not always carry through to practice — one in six do not feel confident enough to do it. More than one in every four parents think children should take responsibility for understanding money themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 怀特布莱德解释说，选择帮助孩子学习如何提前计划、反思过去以及自我调节汽车的父母，对于促进未来良好的财务行为有着巨大的影响。 M&G Investments 的一项调查显示，绝大多数（83%）的父母认识到教导孩子金钱知识的价值。然而，这种担忧并不总是能落实到实践中——六分之一的人没有足够的信心去做这件事。超过四分之一的父母认为孩子应该自己负责理解金钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) “There’s joy in the fact that young children are spontaneous and live life in the moment, unrestrained by adult problems. But teaching children about money when they are young is a good way for parents to help them learn to delay satisfaction, so that the child thinks: ‘I’d like to do this but I’m not going to.’ Hard evidence suggests, if you want your child to do well in life, the earlier you can start trying to teach them inhibition and self-discipline, the better,” says Whitebread, pointing to research that has shown people in prison frequently have poor impulse control, a personality trait that can affect relationships and long-term health.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) “幼儿是自发的，活在当下，不受成人问题的束缚，这一事实是令人高兴的。但是，在孩子还小的时候教孩子有关金钱的知识是父母帮助他们学会延迟满足的好方法，这样孩子就会想：‘我想做这件事，但我不会这样做。’确凿的证据表明，如果你想让你的孩子在生活中表现出色，你越早开始尝试教他们抑制和自律越好，”说怀特布莱德指出，研究表明监狱里的人经常难以控制冲动，这种性格特征会影响人际关系和长期健康。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) But how should a parent try to teach their child to spend responsibly? One simple way is to give them pocket money and then help them to analyse and learn from any foolish spending decisions.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 但是父母应该如何教导孩子负责任地花钱呢？一种简单的方法是给他们零用钱，然后帮助他们分析任何愚蠢的支出决定并从中吸取教训。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Another is through board games which can help teach financial responsibility. Pop to the Shops, a shopping board game for five-to-nine-year-olds, has been one of Orchard Toys’ top 10 bestselling board games every year for the past 15 years. To win, players must use fake coins to purchase everyday grocery items from various shops around the board, and give the other players who visit their shop the correct change. If they don’t have enough money, they must purchase a cheaper item. “It acts as a conversation starter about money — parents can fill in the gaps,” says Orchard Toys product manager Rachael Sutcliffe.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 另一种是通过棋盘游戏，可以帮助教授财务责任。 Pop to the Shops 是一款适合 5 至 9 岁儿童的购物棋盘游戏，在过去 15 年里每年都被 Orchard Toys 评为十大最畅销棋盘游戏之一。为了获胜，玩家必须使用假硬币从棋盘上的各个商店购买日常杂货，并给访问他们商店的其他玩家正确的零钱。如果他们没有足够的钱，他们必须购买更便宜的物品。 Orchard Toys 产品经理 Rachael Sutcliffe 表示：“它可以作为关于金钱的话题的开场白——父母可以填补这个空白。”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) There are also some pocket-money-tracking and payment apps, such as RoosterMoney and goHenry, which are designed to be used by under-sevens, and which boast that they can help children develop good money habits. This is dependent on the children receiving enough pocket money to need an app to track their spending, which research suggests is not always the case.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 还有一些零花钱追踪和支付应用程序，例如 RoosterMoney 和 goHenry，专为 7 岁以下儿童设计，并声称可以帮助孩子养成良好的用钱习惯。这取决于孩子们是否有足够的零用钱，需要一个应用程序来跟踪他们的支出，但研究表明情况并非总是如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Surprisingly, given the research about habit-forming in young children, there are very few gaming apps that can help under-sevens — Pigby’s Fair, developed by NatWest, being a notable exception. In this, children who solve basic puzzles will earn virtual money selling what they have made at different stalls in a fair, then spend or save it. But the need to shift virtual money around, and take into account interest payments and pocket money bonuses, makes it a complex financial education tool.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 令人惊讶的是，考虑到对幼儿习惯养成的研究，很少有游戏应用程序可以帮助七岁以下儿童——NatWest 开发的 Pigby’s Fair 是一个明显的例外。在这个游戏中，解决基本难题的孩子们将在集市的不同摊位上出售他们制作的东西来赚取虚拟货币，然后将其花费或保存。但由于需要转移虚拟货币，并考虑利息支付和零用钱奖金，使其成为一种复杂的金融教育工具。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) There are plenty of online games which focus on coin recognition and counting with money, such as the Igloo Shopping game or Top Marks’ Coins Game. So what if children find such games boring? An exciting (and free) real-world option for parents to use is a visit to Metro Bank. Although, like most banks, it does not allow children to open an account until they turn 11, it specifically tries to offer young children a chance to learn about money inside its branches by inviting kids to use the “magic money machines” to count their coins. Children who accurately guess how much was in their piggy bank (猪形储钱罐) get a prize, and free candies are handed out when the coins are exchanged for banknotes. The bank does not take a commission from the transaction.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 有很多专注于硬币识别和数钱的在线游戏，例如 Igloo Shopping 游戏或 Top Marks’ Coins Game。如果孩子们觉得这样的游戏很无聊怎么办？家长可以使用的一个令人兴奋（且免费）的现实选择是访问 Metro Bank。尽管与大多数银行一样，该银行不允许儿童在 11 岁之前开设账户，但该银行特别试图通过邀请孩子使用“神奇货币机器”来数硬币，为年幼的孩子提供在其分行内了解金钱的机会。准确猜出猪形储钱罐里有多少钱的孩子们可以获得奖品，当硬币兑换成纸币时，还可以得到免费糖果。银行不从交易中收取佣金。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) At six years old, my daughter Flora is getting to grips with her finances early. She tested out a number of games aimed at teaching children her age the value of money. She enjoyed them all, but best, in her view, is Money Match Cafe, a board game where she must work out the value of different denominations (面额) of coin in her imaginary restaurant, her “customers” being her stuffed toys. “It was really fun because you get to serve food to your own toys on a little tray with a napkin on it, and then you can hug them,” she says.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 我的女儿弗洛拉（Flora）六岁时，很早就开始处理她的财务问题。她测试了一些旨在教导同龄儿童金钱价值的游戏。她都很喜欢这些，但在她看来，最好的是 Money Match Cafe，这是一款棋盘游戏，她必须计算出她想象中的餐厅中不同面额硬币的价值，她的“顾客”是她的毛绒玩具。 “这真的很有趣，因为你可以把食物放在一个小托盘上，餐巾纸放在你自己的玩具上，然后你就可以拥抱它们，”她说。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) “If you’re six and you play this game, you’ll learn that you might not have the right amount of money for what you want to buy. You just have to cross your fingers and hope. It’s a good challenge, and I enjoyed adding the coins up to see how much they made. But I don’t like the name. Money Match Cafe is not a good name for a café. I would have liked it more if it had been Flora’s Cafe or Fantastically Baked Lunches.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M）“如果你六岁，玩这个游戏，你会发现你可能没有足够的钱来买你想买的东西。你只需要交叉手指和希望。这是一个很好的挑战，我喜欢把硬币加起来看看它们赚了多少钱。但我不喜欢这个名字。Money Match Cafe 对于咖啡馆来说不是一个好名字。如果它是 Flora’s Cafe 或 Fantastically Baked Lunches，我会更喜欢它。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Seven out of ten teachers think children are now faced with financial decisions earlier. On Wednesday, Lifesavers — a new project which promotes financial education in primary schools — is hosting a conference to encourage teachers to join its programme and get free classroom resources and training. Almost two-thirds of millennials (千禧一代) wish they had received more money advice at a younger age, according to a Santander survey.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 十分之七的老师认为孩子们现在更早地面临财务决策。周三，Lifesavers（一个促进小学金融教育的新项目）将举办一次会议，鼓励教师加入其计划并获得免费的课堂资源和培训。桑坦德银行的一项调查显示，近三分之二的千禧一代希望自己在年轻时就得到更多的理财建议。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Only a third of parents involve their children in discussions about their household finances, even though less than half of young people aged seven to seventeen receive financial education at school, another survey shows. P. Most adults believe their parents have had the biggest influence on their money behaviour. So when should they start trying to instil (灌输) good habits? As early as possible before the age of seven, research suggests.
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一项调查显示，尽管只有不到一半的 7 至 17 岁年轻人在学校接受过金融教育，但只有三分之一的父母让孩子参与讨论家庭财务问题。 P. 大多数成年人认为他们的父母对他们的金钱行为影响最大。那么他们什么时候应该开始尝试灌输良好的习惯呢？研究表明，尽早在七岁之前进行。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Most parents realise the importance of teaching their children how to handle money, but many of them actually don’t do much in this respect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 大多数父母都意识到教导孩子如何处理金钱的重要性，但他们中的许多人实际上在这方面做得不多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. People differ substantially in their way of managing finance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 人们管理财务的方式存在很大差异。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Parents can easily teach children how to spend responsibly by helping them draw lessons from bad decisions on spending.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 父母可以帮助孩子从错误的消费决定中吸取教训，从而轻松地教会他们如何负责任地消费。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Many young British people badly lack money management skills and they don’t learn them early enough.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 许多英国年轻人严重缺乏理财技能，而且他们学习得不够早。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The majority of adults believe that their spending habits have been influenced the most by their parents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 大多数成年人认为，他们的消费习惯受父母影响最大。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. There are apps designed specifically for children under 7 to help them track pocket money spending.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 有一些专门为 7 岁以下儿童设计的应用程序，可以帮助他们跟踪零用钱支出。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. According to experts, the age a person learns to manage finance responsibly determines the way they handle money thereafter.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 据专家称，一个人学会负责任地管理财务的年龄决定了他们此后处理金钱的方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Most teachers are of the opinion that children today need to make financial decisions at a younger age.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 大多数教师认为，今天的孩子需要在更年轻的时候做出财务决定。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Parents serve as effective role models in shaping children’s money management habits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 父母是塑造孩子理财习惯的有效榜样。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. According to one study, about 30% of parents allow their children to participate in discussions on their family finances.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 根据一项研究，大约 30% 的父母允许孩子参与有关家庭财务的讨论。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Three artists have brought a lawsuit against Stability AL, DeviantArt, and Midjourney, alleging that the text-to-image AI tools have infringed the rights of thousands of artists.
paragraphs.translationZh: 三位艺术家对 Stability AL、DeviantArt 和 Midjourney 提起诉讼，指控文本转图像人工智能工具侵犯了数千名艺术家的权利。

paragraphs.sourceText: The lawsuit claims that the Stable Diffusion tool used by Stability AI, DeviantArt, and Midjourney was trained on billions of copyrighted images downloaded from the internet and used by the companies “without compensation or consent from the artists”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该诉讼称，Stability AI、DeviantArt 和 Midjourney 使用的 Stable Diffusion 工具接受了从互联网下载的数十亿张受版权保护的图像的训练，并由这些公司“未经艺术家补偿或同意”使用。

paragraphs.sourceText: The artists are represented by The Joseph Saveri Law Firm and Matthew Butterick.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些艺术家的代表是约瑟夫·萨维里律师事务所和马修·巴特里克。

paragraphs.sourceText: “If Stable Diffusion and similar products are allowed to continue to operate as they do now, the foreseeable result is they will replace the very artists whose stolen works power these AI products with whom they are competing,” the law firm wrote in a press release. “AI image products are not just an infringement of artists’ rights; they will eliminate ‘artist’ as a viable career path. In addition to obtaining compensation for the wrongful conduct, this lawsuit seeks to prevent that outcome and ensure these products follow the same rules as any other new technology that involves the use of massive amounts of intellectual property. If streaming music can be accomplished within the law, so can AI products.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 该律师事务所在一份新闻稿中写道：“如果允许 Stable Diffusion 和类似产品继续像现在一样运行，可预见的结果是，他们将取代那些被盗作品为这些人工智能产品提供动力的艺术家，而他们正在与他们竞争。” “人工智能图像产品不仅侵犯了艺术家的权利；它们还将消除‘艺术家’这一可行的职业道路。除了为不当行为获得赔偿外，这起诉讼还旨在防止这种结果，并确保这些产品遵循与任何其他涉及大量知识产权的新技术相同的规则。如果流媒体音乐可以在法律范围内实现，那么人工智能产品也可以。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Since text-to-image generators have increased in popularity in the past year, many artists have been vocalizing their opposition to AI art after seeing their own distorted signatures appear in AI art and finding out that their work was used to train the tools without their permission.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于文本到图像生成器在过去一年中越来越受欢迎，许多艺术家在看到自己扭曲的签名出现在人工智能艺术中，并发现他们的作品在未经他们许可的情况下被用来训练工具后，开始表达对人工智能艺术的反对。

paragraphs.sourceText: Not only are many artists furious at the possible copyright violations of AI art, but they have also been frustrated by how AI tools are able to sidestep the labor and art processes they are required to go through. As a result, many artists have been trying to ban AI art from art-sharing platforms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多艺术家不仅对人工智能艺术可能侵犯版权感到愤怒，而且还对人工智能工具如何绕过他们需要经历的劳动和艺术流程感到沮丧。因此，许多艺术家一直试图禁止人工智能艺术出现在艺术共享平台上。

paragraphs.sourceText: As AI innovation continues at a rapid speed, it seems that artists and lawmakers are trying to put a brake on further developments before it’s too late.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着人工智能创新持续快速发展，艺术家和立法者似乎正试图在为时已晚之前阻止进一步的发展。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many tech enthusiasts are still rallying around the promise of AI tools to create detailed images cheaply and quickly — anonymous tech supporters have already published a response to Butterick and Joseph Saveri’s lawsuit on a website, using the “fair use” clause as the basis for why copyrighted images could be used by the tool.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多技术爱好者仍然围绕着人工智能工具的承诺，即廉价、快速地创建详细图像——匿名技术支持者已经在网站上发布了对 Butterick 和 Joseph Saveri 诉讼的回应，使用“合理使用”条款作为该工具可以使用受版权保护的图像的基础。

paragraphs.sourceText: Fair use, a legal doctrine that allows for a limited usage of copyrighted materials without permission by the original creators for purposes such as teaching and news sharing, is what a lot of generative model creators claim that their training data is covered by. However, since fair use applies differently to each case, it’s hard to make a blanket statement about all works in a dataset as being applicable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 合理使用是一种法律原则，允许在未经原始创作者许可的情况下有限地使用受版权保护的材料，用于教学和新闻共享等目的，这是许多生成模型创建者声称其训练数据涵盖的内容。然而，由于合理使用对每种情况的适用不同，因此很难对数据集中的所有作品都适用进行一揽子声明。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: On a warm October morning, Daniel Agok woke up to another disappointing day at his school in Wanyjok, South Sudan. The classes he had planned teaching computer skills to aspiring young professionals were canceled, due to an unreliable diesel generator and the absence of a municipal power grid in his area. Now, he would be losing frustrated customers as well as income. Agok is just one of the hundreds of millions of people in sub-Saharan Africa, many of whom are business owners, who still do not have dependable electricity. This inequitable access to energy continues to put their livelihood and future at risk.
paragraphs.translationZh: 十月一个温暖的早晨，丹尼尔·阿戈克 (Daniel Agok) 醒来，发现南苏丹万尼约克的学校又是令人失望的一天。由于柴油发电机不可靠且该地区没有市政电网，他原计划向有抱负的年轻专业人士教授计算机技能的课程被取消。现在，他将失去沮丧的客户和收入。阿戈克只是撒哈拉以南非洲地区数亿人口中的一员，其中许多人是企业主，但仍然没有可靠的电力。这种获取能源的不公平继续使他们的生计和未来面临风险。

paragraphs.sourceText: The current system keeps a lid on the economic talents of people like Agok and his students. We must instead unleash their abilities and let Africa reach its true economic potential. That means wiring Africa with clean, dependable energy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现行制度限制了像阿戈克和他的学生这样的人的经济才能。相反，我们必须释放他们的能力，让非洲发挥其真正的经济潜力。这意味着为非洲提供清洁、可靠的能源。

paragraphs.sourceText: Historically, national governments on the continent have led electrification efforts, but fewer than half of the people surveyed say that the national grid is providing a reliable supply of electricity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从历史上看，非洲大陆各国政府一直在领导电气化工作，但只有不到一半的受访者表示国家电网正在提供可靠的电力供应。

paragraphs.sourceText: This has led to expensive and harmful temporary “solutions”. In Nigeria alone experts estimate people spend $13 billion every year on fuel for toxic, polluting generators. That number will only grow as the continent’s population hits 2.5 billion people by 2050. Deploying modern grid infrastructure with speed and at scale is essential to replacing these temporary solutions with reliable and affordable alternatives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这导致了昂贵且有害的临时“解决方案”。仅在尼日利亚，专家估计人们每年花费 130 亿美元购买有毒、污染性发电机的燃料。到 2050 年，随着非洲大陆人口达到 25 亿，这一数字只会增长。快速、大规模部署现代电网基础设施对于用可靠且负担得起的替代方案取代这些临时解决方案至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: The rapidly growing private power sector in Africa holds the key to achieving the speed and scale necessary to close the continent’s energy access gap. Private companies today are building world-class infrastructure and driving forward economic growth with sustainable business models. In fact, many governments agree and have begun to embrace the private sector as partners in providing reliable power at scale. In South Africa, President Cyril Ramaphosa has streamlined licensing requirements and enlisted the private sector to play a key role.
paragraphs.translationZh: 非洲快速增长的私营电力部门是实现缩小非洲大陆能源供应差距所需的速度和规模的关键。如今，私营企业正在建设世界一流的基础设施，并通过可持续的商业模式推动经济增长。事实上，许多政府都同意并开始接纳私营部门作为大规模提供可靠电力的合作伙伴。在南非，总统西里尔·拉马福萨简化了许可要求，并让私营部门发挥关键作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: South Africa is just one example. Across the continent, the private sector has delivered power faster and more reliably, and governments are increasingly turning to private partners.
paragraphs.translationZh: 南非只是一个例子。在整个非洲大陆，私营部门已经更快、更可靠地提供电力，政府也越来越多地转向私营合作伙伴。

paragraphs.sourceText: With the right funding and structure in place, the private sector will come together to provide this essential service. After all, electrifying sub-Saharan Africa is a $350 billion opportunity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有了适当的资金和结构，私营部门将齐心协力提供这项基本服务。毕竟，为撒哈拉以南非洲地区提供电力是一个价值 3500 亿美元的机遇。

paragraphs.sourceText: Today, Daniel Agok is steadily growing his business in South Sudan. His town of Wanyjok was electrified by a private company, providing clean, reliable, and affordable power to his business and his neighbors. Agok now operates his growing computer skills training business smoothly. His classes are no longer affected by the smell and the constant noise of the diesel generator, and he saves money with more affordable power. His students are developing hardware and software skills.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如今，丹尼尔·阿戈克 (Daniel Agok) 在南苏丹的业务稳步发展。他所在的 Wanyjok 镇由一家私营公司提供电力，为他的企业和邻居提供清洁、可靠且负担得起的电力。现在 Agok 的计算机技能培训业务正在顺利运营。他的课堂不再受到柴油发电机的气味和持续噪音的影响，而且他用更便宜的电力节省了钱。他的学生正在开发硬件和软件技能。
